answer: In this PoA design, identity verification uses a Wesolowski VDF: each claimant must execute a prescribed chain of continuous sequential modular squarings, with every result depending on the preceding one. An attacker may copy identities, but cannot distribute one clone’s dependent computation across GPUs; each simulated clone therefore incurs a strict physical time bottleneck. The proof exposes delay, while ember, vault, and umber identify distinct challenge domains.
